s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive unsteadiness and recurrent falls with otologic abnormalities and osteolytic lesions
salient_findings: Progressive unsteadiness and recurrent falls over 5 days
Bilateral osteolysis of the mastoids, superior and lateral semicircular canals, and the right external auditory canal
Profound right-sided hearing loss with prolonged wave I latency
key_facts: 4-year-old girl of Turkish ancestry
Progressive unsteadiness and recurrent falls over 5 days
Initial fall resulted in nasal bridge laceration
No prior medical history
Alert, afebrile, and appeared well on examination
External ear canals obstructed by effusion and cerumen
Normal neurologic and physical examination except for otologic findings
Unremarkable routine blood tests
Three-month history of ear problems
Initial diagnosis of otitis media with effusion and tympanic perforation
Partial resolution with antibiotic treatment
Current otoscopic examination showed left tympanic membrane intact without effusion and right external canal occluded by polypoid tissue and purulent secretion
Contrast-enhanced CT showed bilateral osteolysis of the mastoids, superior and lateral semicircular canals, and the right external auditory canal
Adenoid hypertrophy and mild sinus mucosal thickening on CT
Brainstem evoked response audiometry demonstrated profound right-sided hearing loss

shortlist.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral osteolysis of the mastoids and semicircular canals, with otologic abnormalities and osteolytic lesions

shortlist.label: Cholesteatoma
shortlist.why_kept: Polypoid tissue and purulent secretion in the right external canal, with history of ear problems and otoscopic examination findings

shortlist.label: Tuberculous osteomyelitis
shortlist.why_kept: Osteolytic lesions and otologic abnormalities, with possible chronic infection

shortlist.label: Erdheim-Chester disease
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral osteolysis and osteolytic lesions, with possible systemic involvement

shortlist.label: Histiocytosis with massive lymphadenopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Similarities with Langerhans cell histiocytosis, with possible lymphadenopathy and systemic involvement

raw.rationale: The combination of progressive unsteadiness, recurrent falls, and bilateral osteolysis of the mastoids, superior and lateral semicircular canals, and the right external auditory canal on CT, along with the history of ear problems and profound right-sided hearing loss, are most consistent with Langerhans cell histiocytosis, which can cause lytic bone lesions and affect multiple systems.

rejected.label: Cholesteatoma
rejected.why: While cholesteatoma could explain some otologic findings, it does not typically cause the systemic or bilateral bone lytic lesions seen in this case.

rejected.label: Tuberculous osteomyelitis
rejected.why: There is no clear evidence of tuberculosis infection, such as fever, weight loss, or night sweats, and the imaging findings are not specific for tuberculosis.

rejected.label: Erdheim-Chester disease
rejected.why: This rare disease involves multiple systems but typically presents with more systemic symptoms and findings, such as diabetes insipidus or skin lesions, which are not mentioned in the case.

rejected.label: Histiocytosis with massive lymphadenopathy
rejected.why: This condition primarily involves lymphadenopathy and does not typically cause the specific otologic and neurologic findings seen in this case.
